top_line: After broad criticism in parliament, Finance Minister Heinen said the cabinet will change its wealth-tax plan to spare small savers and investors. Separately, an Ebola-infected aid worker from Congo is being treated in strict isolation in Leiden, and the EU has halted aid to Sierra Leone amid a dispute over fugitive drug lord Bolle Jos.

stories.headline: Aid worker with Ebola flown from Congo to Leiden hospital
stories.summary: An aid worker for Médecins Sans Frontières (Doctors Without Borders) who was infected with Ebola in the Democratic Republic of Congo is being treated at Leiden University Medical Center (LUMC). The patient was flown in on a French private plane after a flight of about nine and a half hours. The plane landed at Schiphol around 7:45 pm on Thursday, and the patient was driven to Leiden under escort by the Royal Military Police. The national public health institute RIVM says the patient is being kept in strict isolation. The patient's identity, sex, nationality and condition have not been released. Health Minister Sophie Hermans says the LUMC is prepared to receive, screen and treat Ebola patients. The hospital and MSF both say there is no risk to other patients, visitors or the public, and visiting hours are unchanged. The Netherlands has treated an Ebola patient once before: in December 2014 a Nigerian UN peacekeeper from Liberia was cured at UMC Utrecht. The outbreak in Congo was declared in May in Ituri province, which remains the worst-hit area, and has since spread to North Kivu and several other provinces. It is caused by the rare Bundibugyo strain, for which there is no approved vaccine or treatment. It is the largest Ebola outbreak ever recorded in the country, with more than 8,200 confirmed cases and nearly 4,000 deaths. MSF says the true toll is probably higher.
stories.context: Ebola is a severe and often fatal viral disease that spreads through direct contact with the bodily fluids of people who are sick. It does not spread through the air. Western countries regularly bring infected aid workers home for treatment in specialised isolation units, as the US did with patients treated at Emory in Atlanta in 2014. The LUMC is one of the Dutch academic hospitals with high-level isolation facilities and runs regular drills for patients with serious infectious diseases. The RIVM is roughly the Dutch counterpart of the CDC.
key_terms: LUMC, Leids Universitair Medisch Centrum (Leiden University Medical Center)
Artsen zonder Grenzen (Doctors Without Borders / MSF)
RIVM, Rijksinstituut voor Volksgezondheid en Milieu (National Institute for Public Health and the Environment)
Koninklijke Marechaussee (Royal Military Police, which also polices Schiphol and the borders)
Schiphol (Amsterdam's main airport)
open_questions: What is the condition of the MSF aid worker being treated at the LUMC?

findings.question: What is the condition of the MSF aid worker being treated at the LUMC?
Has the Netherlands treated an Ebola patient before, for example the patients brought to the LUMC or Erasmus MC during the 2014 West Africa outbreak?
findings.answer: Yes. In early December 2014 a Nigerian soldier serving with the UN peacekeeping mission in Liberia was flown to Schiphol and treated in strict isolation at UMC Utrecht, not at the LUMC or Erasmus MC. He was the first foreign Ebola patient treated in the Netherlands. He recovered, was discharged on 22 December 2014 and flew back to Liberia. Separately, NOS reported a patient with suspected Ebola being admitted to the LUMC in 2015, but no confirmed earlier Ebola treatment at the LUMC was found.

findings.question: Which part of the DR Congo is the 2026 Ebola outbreak centred in, and which Ebola strain is it?
findings.answer: The outbreak was declared on 14 May 2026 in Ituri province in north-eastern DRC, which remains by far the worst-hit area. According to ECDC, as of 1 October Ituri had 6,250 cases and 2,885 deaths. It has since spread to North Kivu (1,570 cases and 931 deaths), Haut-Uélé, Tshopo, Bas-Uélé, South Kivu and Sud-Ubangi, affecting 63 health zones. It is caused by the Bundibugyo virus, a rare Ebola species for which there is no approved vaccine or treatment. ECDC's total as of 1 October is 8,224 confirmed cases and 3,982 deaths. Three imported cases in Germany and France have all recovered.

stories.headline: Cabinet backs down on taxing small savers in box 3
stories.previously: On the first day of the budget debate, opposition parties and even the coalition's own MPs rejected the plan to cut the tax-free return in box 3 to €1,000 from 2028, a measure meant to raise €473 million.
stories.summary: On the second day of the budget debate, Finance Minister Eelco Heinen said the minority cabinet is willing to change the wealth-tax plan so that small savers and investors are spared. He called the criticism a "clear signal" from the House. Heinen said he had chosen the €1,000 threshold, down from the current €1,800, because it would still exempt a couple with up to about €100,000 in savings. He admitted he had underestimated how many people who pay no tax on their savings now would start paying; estimates put the number of extra taxpayers at around 850,000. "We are prepared to set a different threshold," he said, but he did not name a new figure or say how it would be paid for. He warned that finding the same money elsewhere is "enormously complicated" because the cabinet has "not many dials to turn." He also said he would look again at next year's temporary measure, which would cut the tax-free allowance from €59,357 to €30,846 per person and raise the assumed return on investments, though he made no firm commitment to drop it. He wants clarity by the Tax Plan debate in two weeks. On the fallback cut to education, which could reach €1.2 billion a year from 2031, Heinen said the saving is "technically booked" but will never happen if employers and unions reach a social accord. He expects such an accord to save more on unemployment and disability benefits (WW and WIA) than the cabinet's original cuts. The cabinet still has to find about €3 billion in savings. Education Minister Letschert said on Wednesday that there is no coalition agreement to cut education.
stories.context: The 'polder' refers to the Dutch habit of settling economic policy through consensus talks between the government, employers and trade unions. A 'social accord' is a deal reached that way. Because the cabinet is a minority government, it needs opposition votes to pass its budget, which gives opposition parties real leverage.
key_terms: Algemene Financiële Beschouwingen (annual general debate on the budget and finances)
Belastingplan (Tax Plan, the annual package of tax legislation)
sociaal akkoord (social accord between employers and unions)
de polder / poldermodel (Dutch consensus-based decision-making)
WW (unemployment benefit) and WIA (long-term disability benefit)
Letschert (Education Minister)
open_questions: How much do employers and unions say a social accord would save on WW and WIA benefits, and by when must it be agreed?

findings.question: What new box 3 threshold, if any, has Heinen proposed in place of the €1,000 tax-free return, and how would it be paid for?
findings.answer: He has not proposed one yet. Heinen said he is prepared to set a different threshold than €1,000 (currently €1,800) and wants clarity by the Tax Plan debate in about two weeks. He gave no new figure and no way to pay for it. He said finding the money elsewhere is 'enormously complicated' and that he has 'not many dials to turn'. Commentators note that small savers were the main source of funding for the box 3 overhaul, so the financing remains open.

findings.question: How much do employers and unions say a social accord would save on WW and WIA benefits, and by when must it be agreed?
Will the cabinet also drop or soften the 2027 cut to the tax-free allowance, from €59,357 to €30,846?
findings.answer: Not yet decided. Heinen said he would look again at the temporary 2027 measures, but De Belegger reports he made no firm commitment. As things stand, the 2027 plan still cuts the allowance from €59,357 to €30,846 per person and raises the assumed investment return to 7.87%. Clarity is expected by the Tax Plan debate in two weeks.

stories.headline: EU halts payments to Sierra Leone, and Dutch minister links it to drug lord Bolle Jos
stories.summary: The European Commission has stopped budget support payments to Sierra Leone with immediate effect. The country was due to receive €18 million this year for food programmes, education and infrastructure. Dutch Justice Minister David van Weel confirmed the move after a report in De Telegraaf. He presented it as a response to Sierra Leone's refusal to extradite fugitive drug lord Jos Leijdekkers, known as 'Bolle Jos'. He said the country "can solve this within 24 hours" by arresting and extraditing him. The Netherlands also wants a further €22.5 million payment due next year to be stopped, and EU member states are still negotiating over it. NOS reports that Van Weel's comments irritated the Commission. Officially, the Commission says the suspension is purely technical and caused by "administrative errors", and some there called the minister's framing misleading. Magnus Brunner, the EU Commissioner for Internal Affairs and Migration, said the reasons were "technical" but did not elaborate, saying the matter falls outside his portfolio. He did add: "We need Sierra Leone's cooperation. That is what this is about." Budget support agreements are binding contracts. The extradition is not one of their conditions, so suspending payments over it would not be legally allowed. Sierra Leone's Information Minister Chernor Bah said the 2026 support was delayed by procedural matters involving an amended financing agreement, with payments now proposed for 2027 and 2028. He said a punitive framing does not reflect the reasons formally given to his government, which also says EU officials told it the suspension was unrelated to any specific person. The government called public pressure and media campaigns "not conducive" to judicial cooperation. The Netherlands and Sierra Leone have no bilateral extradition treaty. Both are parties to the UN Convention against Transnational Organized Crime, however, and it contains an extradition provision. In Luxembourg, EU justice ministers discussed tougher sanctions, such as entry bans and asset freezes, for criminals hiding outside Europe.
stories.context: Jos Leijdekkers is often called the most wanted criminal in the Low Countries. He was sentenced in absentia to 24 years in the Netherlands for cocaine trafficking and an attempted murder, and in Belgium to more than 100 years in total across several cases. He is reported to have a child with the daughter of Sierra Leone's president, Julius Maada Bio, and close ties to the government. The Netherlands and Sierra Leone have no easy extradition route. The Dutch government treats the cocaine trade as a national security issue. Pressure has grown since a deadly armed attack last month on a farm in Overasselt, Gelderland, which is believed to be linked to the drug trade. Van Weel is from the VVD, the centre-right liberal party.
key_terms: Bolle Jos ('Chubby Jos', nickname of Jos Leijdekkers)
Van Weel (Justice and Security Minister)
begrotingssteun (budget support, aid paid directly into a government's budget)
Europese Commissie (European Commission, the EU's executive)
Overasselt (Gelderland village hit by drug-related violence)
De Telegraaf (Dutch tabloid newspaper)

findings.question: What 'administrative errors' does the European Commission cite for suspending budget support to Sierra Leone?
findings.answer: The Commission has not said what the errors are. NOS reports only that it officially calls the suspension a technical matter caused by "administrative errors". Commissioner Brunner cited "technical reasons" but declined to elaborate. Sierra Leone's Information Minister Chernor Bah gave his government's account: he said the 2026 budget support was delayed by procedural matters involving an amended financing agreement, with disbursements proposed for 2027 and 2028. He also said the punitive framing does not reflect the reasons formally given to Sierra Leone. Note on next year's payment: Brussels Signal reports €20.5 million, but NOS and Reuters both say €22.5 million.

findings.question: Which EU Commissioner is Brunner, and what is his portfolio?
findings.answer: Magnus Brunner, the European Commissioner for Internal Affairs (and Migration). He said the budget support was suspended for "technical reasons" but would not go further because development aid is not his portfolio. He stressed EU concerns about drug trafficking and organised crime in Sierra Leone. EU foreign affairs chief Kaja Kallas had earlier raised the issue with Sierra Leone's foreign minister at the UN General Assembly.

findings.question: Is there an extradition treaty or legal basis for Sierra Leone to extradite Jos Leijdekkers to the Netherlands?
findings.answer: There is no bilateral extradition treaty between the Netherlands and Sierra Leone. Both countries are parties to the UN Convention against Transnational Organized Crime, which contains an extradition provision, so a request can be made on that basis. Whether to extradite remains largely a political decision for the requested state, and extradition cannot go ahead if the person risks mistreatment.

findings.question: Which countries did Van Weel visit on his recent West Africa trip, and what came of the proposed permanent secretariat on drug shipments?
findings.answer: Partly confirmed. In July 2026 Van Weel visited Ghana to build a coalition of West African countries to pressure Sierra Leone, and to propose a permanent secretariat in West Africa to tackle drug-smuggling networks. No other countries on the trip could be confirmed. No report found says the secretariat has been set up; it is still described as a plan.

stories.headline: Katwijk approves Eli Lilly's $3 billion pill factory
stories.summary: The municipal council of Katwijk, a coastal town near Leiden, voted 28 to 4 on Thursday evening to approve a building permit for a $3 billion factory by the US pharmaceutical company Eli Lilly. Local parties KiesKatwijk and GemeenteBelangen were among those who opposed it. The plant, near the Valkenburgse Meer lake, will make oral medicines for diabetes and weight loss, including Lilly's GLP-1 pill orforglipron. It is expected to employ about 500 people. Earlier the same evening, the council rejected a request from hundreds of residents for an advisory referendum on the project, partly because the municipality had to decide on the permit this week. Lilly still needs permits to start production and to discharge wastewater. When it announced the plan eleven months ago, the company said it expected construction to start in 2026 and production to begin in 2030. Because the power grid has no spare capacity for the coming years, the company will initially generate its own electricity with gas turbines. CEO David Ricks cited the nearby airports and the Leiden Bio Science Park as reasons for choosing Katwijk. Many residents worry about water and energy use, safety, and the effect on views and recreation at the lake. The plant is expected to use about 800,000 litres of drinking water a day, roughly as much as all the households in the neighbouring village of Valkenburg. Most of the council judged that the economic benefits outweigh these concerns.
stories.context: Eli Lilly makes some of the world's best-selling diabetes and obesity drugs, and the large investment fits the global race to build production capacity for them. Grid congestion ('netcongestie') is a major issue in the Netherlands: across much of the country, new businesses must wait years for a grid connection, which is why the factory will burn gas for its own power. In the Netherlands, local councils decide on building permits, much like zoning boards in the US.
key_terms: Katwijk (coastal town in South Holland, near Leiden)
Valkenburgse Meer (lake near Katwijk)
gemeenteraad (municipal council)
Leiden Bio Science Park (life sciences cluster in Leiden)
netcongestie (grid congestion)
Omroep West (regional broadcaster for The Hague and Leiden area)

findings.question: Which Eli Lilly drugs will the Katwijk factory produce, for example the oral GLP-1 pill orforglipron?
findings.answer: The plant will make oral medicines, especially orforglipron, Lilly's oral GLP-1 drug for obesity and diabetes. According to European Pharmaceutical Review, it will also produce some of Lilly's oral medicines for neuroscience, oncology and immunology. Dutch outlets describe its output as diabetes and weight-loss pills.

findings.question: When does Eli Lilly expect construction in Katwijk to start and production to begin?
findings.answer: When Lilly announced the plant in November 2025, it said construction would start in 2026, subject to permits, and production would begin in 2030. No updated timeline turned up in reporting on Thursday's vote. Lilly still needs production and wastewater-discharge permits.

findings.question: Which four Katwijk council members or parties voted against the Eli Lilly permit?
findings.answer: Only partly confirmed. Allesoverkatwijk's liveblog of the vote, which was available only as a summary, names KiesKatwijk (Gijsbert Schrijvers) and GemeenteBelangen (René Slootweg) among the opponents of the 28–4 vote. It mentions CDA only in connection with its support for a referendum, so the full list of four could not be confirmed. In June's provisional vote (26–5), KiesKatwijk, GemeenteBelangen and three of CDA's seven members voted against. NOS and Omroep West do not name the opponents.

findings.question: How much water will the Katwijk plant use per year?
findings.answer: About 800,000 litres (roughly 800 m³) of drinking water a day, roughly the same as all the households in Valkenburg combined (about 6,000 residents), according to local news site Allesoverkatwijk (14 June 2026). That works out to roughly 290,000 m³ a year. This annual figure is a calculation and was not stated by an official source.

stories.headline: Draft law sets clear test for who counts as a freelancer
stories.summary: Minister of Work and Participation Thierry Aartsen has published the draft Self-Employed Persons Act (Zelfstandigenwet), which aims to end years of uncertainty over who counts as a genuine freelancer. The draft sets two tests: a self-employment test and a work-relationship test. Under the draft, you are an entrepreneur if you work independently, carry business risk and are free to organise your own work. In practice, that means being registered with the Chamber of Commerce, having a VAT number and a business bank account, sending invoices, having at least three different clients over two years, and actively seeking new ones. Freelancers must in principle be free to decide where, when and how they work, unless the job can only be done at a specific place, such as a building site, or a specific time. They must also spend a minimum amount on things employees don't need, such as disability insurance, a pension or liability cover. The minimum amount is still to be discussed with business groups. Aartsen said the amount must not be too high but also must not become a "wassen neus" (an empty gesture). He called the criteria "not unreasonable" and estimated that roughly two-thirds to three-quarters of freelancers already meet them or could do so fairly easily. The cabinet puts the number of zzp'ers at more than one million. Anyone meeting the criteria will no longer have to fear back-tax claims. The rules would apply to both existing and new working arrangements, with no transition period. Most freelancer and industry groups have welcomed the plan in principle. ZZP Nederland supports its aims but says the criteria must be clear and workable, and warns that clients must not end up shutting out freelancers anyway to be safe. The union FNV Zelfstandigen has been sceptical: earlier this year it said it saw "no added value" in a Zelfstandigenwet, and that it was unclear on pensions and disability cover. The public can comment on the draft until 29 October, and the law will take effect no earlier than 1 January 2028.
stories.context: About one in eight Dutch workers is a zzp'er, a self-employed person without staff. The tax authority has cracked down on 'schijnzelfstandigheid', or false self-employment, where someone works like an employee but is hired as a freelancer to avoid payroll taxes and benefits. Clients risk back-claims for taxes and social contributions, so many stopped hiring freelancers altogether. This resembles the US debate over contractor misclassification, such as California's AB5 law and the gig economy.
key_terms: zzp'er, zelfstandige zonder personeel (freelancer / self-employed without staff)
schijnzelfstandigheid (false self-employment)
Zelfstandigenwet (Self-Employed Persons Act)
naheffing (back-tax assessment)
Kamer van Koophandel, KvK (Chamber of Commerce, the business register)
Belastingdienst (Dutch tax authority)
Aartsen (Minister of Work and Participation)
internetconsultatie (public online consultation on draft laws)

findings.question: How many zzp'ers are there in the Netherlands, and how many might fail the three-client test?
findings.answer: According to the cabinet, the Netherlands has more than one million zzp'ers. Trade outlet TPO notes that CBS data show about 140,000 fewer active zzp'ers than 18 months ago. I found no official estimate of how many would fail the three-client test specifically. Minister Aartsen said that roughly two-thirds to three-quarters of freelancers already meet the law's criteria or could do so fairly easily, which suggests roughly a quarter to a third currently don't. That figure covers all the criteria, not just the client count.

findings.question: How have freelancer associations and unions such as FNV reacted to the draft Zelfstandigenwet?
findings.answer: I found no published reactions from organisations to the 1 October draft itself; the consultation has only just opened. Earlier positions: ZZP Nederland (14 September 2026, when the cabinet announced its timeline) backs the aims but says success depends on the details. It wants the criteria to be clear, practical and workable, and warns the law must not lead clients to exclude all freelancers out of caution. It plans to submit comments during the consultation. FNV Zelfstandigen (February 2026, reacting to the coalition plans) said through Gery de Boer that it was 'extremely sceptical' and saw 'no added value' in a Zelfstandigenwet. It would rather see existing bills such as VBAR and BAZ passed quickly, and called the law unclear on pensions and disability insurance. In that same round, most other freelancer and industry groups, including VZN, ABU, Bovib and RIM, were positive.

stories.headline: Rivers so low that skippers must judge for themselves whether they can sail
stories.summary: Water levels in the east of the Netherlands are now so low that Rijkswaterstaat, the national waterways agency, can no longer properly measure whether ships can pass safely. This applies to the IJssel, the Nederrijn, the Pannerdensch Kanaal and much of the Waal. In places the water is shallower than 125 centimetres, and most of the agency's survey boats sit deeper than that. Only three shallower boats remain, and they are also needed elsewhere. That means the agency cannot determine the shallowest point in the shipping channel, which skippers use to decide how much cargo they can carry without running aground. Skippers must now decide for themselves, unless they pay for commercial data. Since 25 September, ships on the Upper IJssel have only been allowed to sail one way at a time, and some ships are taking detours of up to 300 kilometres. Fiona Oomen of the inland shipping association called the situation "very worrying" and said all transport, by road and water, is under pressure. The port of Rotterdam says about half as much cargo is moving between Rotterdam and destinations on the Rhine as a year ago. Ships are sailing partly loaded, and freight prices have soared. Industry data showed the cost of shipping a tonne from Rotterdam to Cologne rose from about 17 euros in mid-June to 80 euros in early August. Container carriers are also charging low-water surcharges. The Rhine's flow at Lobith, where it enters the Netherlands, is around 545 cubic metres per second, well below August's record low of 614. Rijkswaterstaat says rain is needed in the river basin, mostly outside the country, and that things will not get much worse but not much better either. It warns that an unusually warm sea could bring a very wet autumn and high water afterwards.
stories.context: The Rhine and its Dutch branches (the Waal, Nederrijn and IJssel) are major freight routes connecting the port of Rotterdam to Germany. Barges carry huge volumes of bulk goods, and low water forces them to sail partly loaded, which raises costs. It is similar to low water on the Mississippi disrupting grain barges. Rijkswaterstaat, part of the infrastructure ministry, manages national roads and waterways, roughly like the US Army Corps of Engineers.
key_terms: Rijkswaterstaat (national roads and waterways agency)
IJssel, Nederrijn, Waal (branches of the Rhine in the Netherlands)
Pannerdensch Kanaal (canal where the Rhine splits)
Lobith (border village where the Rhine enters the Netherlands)
minst gepeilde diepte (least sounded depth, the shallowest measured point in the channel)
binnenvaart (inland shipping)
Koninklijke Binnenvaart Nederland (Royal Dutch inland shipping association)
open_questions: Have any ships run aground on the IJssel or Waal since Rijkswaterstaat stopped measuring depths?

findings.question: Have any ships run aground on the IJssel or Waal since Rijkswaterstaat stopped measuring depths?
How much have barge freight surcharges for low water risen on the Rhine?
findings.answer: No single current figure was found for the Dutch stretch, but several sources show steep rises. Wood Mackenzie data, cited by vesseltracker.com on 17 August 2026, showed barge freight from Rotterdam to Cologne at €80 per tonne in the week ending 7 August, up from €17 in mid-June. Rotterdam to Frankfurt rose from €29 to €150 per tonne over the same period. A Tank Terminals market report for 7–11 September said Rhine tanker rates 'rose in nearly every session' and were nearing their August peaks, but gave no figures. A claim in search snippets that rates 'more than doubled' in September could not be checked. Container carrier Hapag-Lloyd has revised its Rhine low-water surcharges from 1 November 2026, based on the Kaub, Cologne, Duisburg-Ruhrort and Emmerich gauges. At Kaub they run from €40 per 20-foot container (water level 150–131 cm) up to €1,350 at 25 cm or below. At Emmerich they reach €345 per 20-foot and €475 per 40-foot container. TPO also reports that, according to the port of Rotterdam, about half as much cargo is moving between Rotterdam and Rhine destinations as a year ago, which pushes up costs.

stories.headline: Young Amsterdammers drink less but use more ketamine and 3-MMC
stories.summary: The annual Antenne Amsterdam monitor, commissioned by Jellinek's prevention service and published by the Amsterdam University of Applied Sciences (HvA), finds that young people in Amsterdam are drinking less. At the same time, ketamine use in nightlife has risen sharply since 2024. The report draws on a survey of 1,183 vocational (MBO) students, interviews with nightlife insiders and youth workers, and nearly 5,000 drug samples handed in for testing. Ketamine, MDMA and other powders sell for about €25 to €30 a gram and are easy to get through home delivery. Demand for the synthetic stimulant 3-MMC seems barely affected by a ban that took effect in July 2025, and pills sold as 3-MMC often contain other substances. Jellinek says 3-MMC carries a higher risk of dependence than ecstasy. Laughing gas has nearly disappeared since it was banned in 2023. Among MBO students, 59% drank alcohol in the past year. About half have ever vaped and 7% used snus (nicotine pouches). Online gambling is becoming more normal. Twenty-one percent of MBO students have ever gambled online, 18% did so in the past year and 11% in the past four weeks. The past-year share was 6% in 2021, but the researchers warn the comparison is rough because the question was worded differently in 2025. Jellinek's Jacqueline Krouwel said the study does not show that young people are swapping alcohol for cheaper drugs. Gen Z is simply drinking less overall.
stories.context: Jellinek is Amsterdam's best-known addiction treatment and prevention organisation. The Netherlands takes a public-health approach to drugs: it tolerates cannabis in coffeeshops and runs drug-testing services where users can hand in samples anonymously. That testing data feeds monitors like this one. MBO is the vocational track of Dutch education, comparable to community or trade college. Online gambling was legalised in 2021, and its spread among young people has been a political concern ever since. Jellinek's helpline is 088 505 1220, staffed in Dutch and English on weekdays from 1 to 5 pm.
key_terms: Jellinek (Amsterdam addiction care organisation)
Antenne Amsterdam (annual drug and alcohol monitor)
HvA, Hogeschool van Amsterdam (Amsterdam University of Applied Sciences)
mbo (vocational education)
3-MMC (synthetic stimulant)
snus (nicotine pouches, banned in the Netherlands)
Opiumwet (Opium Act, the Dutch drugs law)
Het Parool (Amsterdam newspaper)

findings.question: What are the correct online gambling figures for MBO students in Antenne Amsterdam 2025? NL Times reports 21% have ever gambled online, up from 11% the year before. DutchNews reports 18% gambled online in the past year, up from 6% in 2021, and notes the question was worded differently.
findings.answer: Both outlets' headline figures appear in the HvA press release (30 September 2026), but they measure different things. 21% of MBO students have ever gambled online, 18% did so in the past 12 months and 11% in the past four weeks. Offline, 17% have ever gambled and 12% did so in the past year. The release says past-year online gambling tripled from 6% in 2021 to 18% in 2025, with the caveat that the question was worded differently in 2025. The 11% is the past-four-weeks figure, not a figure from the previous year. NL Times' 'up from 11%' looks like a misreading, and DutchNews' framing is correct.

findings.question: Did the Antenne Amsterdam 2025 report survey nightlife-goers aged 18 to 27, as NL Times says, or does the survey part cover only MBO students, as DutchNews describes?
findings.answer: The HvA press release lists only one survey, of 1,183 MBO students. The nightlife findings come from interviews with professionals and insiders from Amsterdam's nightlife scene and from nearly 5,000 drug samples handed in for testing. DutchNews also mentions interviews with 22 nightlife insiders and five youth workers. The release does not mention a survey of nightlife-goers aged 18 to 27. The previous edition (2024) did survey café-goers, which may explain NL Times' description.

stories.headline: Nijmegen surgeons pioneer clitoris reconstruction after vulvar cancer
stories.summary: Doctors at Radboudumc, the university hospital in Nijmegen, have developed an operation to rebuild the clitoris after part of it is removed because of vulvar cancer. In a first study of 23 women, 90% could again have a clitoral orgasm, three to six months after surgery. The results are published in the journal Gynecologic Oncology. Until now, the wound was simply closed and the clitoris disappeared under a layer of skin. Gynaecological oncologist Mieke ten Eikelder and plastic surgeon Tim Nijhuis, who specialises in gender surgery, developed the technique after a patient asked whether reconstruction was possible. During the tumour removal, the clitoral nerve bundles are freed and moved to form a new tip, which is covered with tissue from the inside of the cheek. The procedure adds about 15 minutes to the operation, so no second surgery is needed. An 80-year-old artist who was treated, Hanni Braspenning, said losing her clitoris would have meant losing part of her womanhood. Of the roughly 450 Dutch women diagnosed with vulvar cancer each year, about a quarter have a tumour in or around the clitoris, according to the hospital; Ten Eikelder has put the figure at 130 to 150 women. All nine Dutch hospitals that treat vulvar cancer will now learn the technique in a nationwide study co-funded by the Dutch Cancer Society (KWF). The first operation has also been done in London. A comparable reconstruction for men with penile cancer has existed for almost 40 years.
stories.context: The breakthrough feeds a growing Dutch conversation about the gender gap in medicine. Amsterdam UMC gynaecology professor Judith Huirne says diagnosing women-specific conditions such as menstrual disorders, menopause symptoms or pelvic floor problems often takes 8 to 12 years. She says about twenty times more money worldwide goes into research on erectile dysfunction than on endometriosis. Amsterdam UMC opened a women's clinic for its own staff, and nearly 1,000 of its 9,000 female employees have used it. About 450 Dutch women get vulvar cancer each year.
key_terms: Radboudumc (university medical center in Nijmegen)

findings.question: How many Dutch vulvar cancer patients a year have a tumour in or near the clitoris? NOS cites 130 to 150 of about 450 (around 30%), while DutchNews says about 25%.
findings.answer: Both figures come from the source material. Radboudumc's own press release says that of the roughly 450 women diagnosed with vulvar cancer each year in the Netherlands, about a quarter have a tumour involving the clitoris or the area around it. DutchNews uses that figure. In NOS's second article, Ten Eikelder herself gives an estimate of 130 to 150 women a year, which is about 29–33%. The two estimates are close, so the safest wording is 'about a quarter to a third'. Another option is to attribute each figure to its source.

findings.question: Has the Radboudumc clitoral reconstruction study been published in a peer-reviewed journal, and if so, which one?
findings.answer: Yes. The study is published in Gynecologic Oncology, a peer-reviewed journal from Elsevier, under the title 'Clitoral reconstructive surgery for patients with vulvar carcinoma'. The authors are Ten Eikelder M, Veldmate G, Pettai F, Schepels-Franke A, de Hullu J and Nijhuis T, and the DOI is 10.1016/j.ygyno.2026.07.013.

stories.headline: Replica ship Batavia leaves Amsterdam to be put on dry land for good
stories.summary: The Batavia, a full-size reconstruction of a 17th-century Dutch East India Company ship, has made its last voyage. After a week and a half at the NDSM wharf in Amsterdam-Noord, where it was fitted into a steel support frame and placed on a pontoon, tugboats towed it across the IJ on Thursday, drawing crowds of onlookers. It then crossed the Markermeer and moored at Museum Batavialand in Lelystad that afternoon. Today, Friday, the ship is to be driven off the pontoon and over the dike, then set down next to the museum. It is being moved onto land permanently because the hull, which has been in the water for about 30 years, suffers from wood rot. Experts concluded it could no longer stay afloat. The ship will be restored in stages, and the museum says it plans to make it safe for visitors to go aboard again. That is expected when the renovated Batavialand reopens in 2028. The cost of the move itself has not been made public. It is part of a museum renovation worth around 25 million euros, paid for by the national government, the province of Flevoland, the municipality of Lelystad and the museum. The original Batavia left Texel for Java in 1628 on its maiden voyage, overshot its course and was wrecked on the reefs of the Houtman Abrolhos islands off Australia. Work on the replica began in 1985, and Queen Beatrix christened it ten years later.
stories.context: The VOC, or Dutch East India Company, was the powerful 17th-century trading company at the heart of the Dutch Golden Age. Its legacy is celebrated as maritime heritage but is also increasingly debated because of its role in colonialism and slavery. The original Batavia is famous for what happened after the wreck: a mutiny and massacre among the survivors. The replica, built by volunteers and apprentices in Lelystad, became a well-known tourist attraction.

findings.question: On what date is the Batavia being driven over the dike and placed next to Batavialand, and can the public watch?
findings.answer: The ship left Amsterdam on Thursday 1 October 2026 and its pontoon moored at Batavialand in Lelystad at about 14:30 that day. NOS (published Thursday) and Omroep Flevoland both say it would be driven off the pontoon and over the dike 'tomorrow' / 'on Friday', meaning Friday 2 October 2026, and placed next to the museum. No source I read said whether the public could watch the move over the dike or set up a viewing area. Earlier reporting said the public could follow the voyage from the water and from points along the shore.

findings.question: Will visitors still be able to go aboard the Batavia once it is on land?
findings.answer: Yes, eventually. The last day to visit the ship while it was still in the water was 30 August 2026. The museum plans to restore the ship in stages, tackling mould and rot and adding three masts and protective covering, and to make it safe and accessible for visitors again. The renovated museum is expected to reopen in 2028: Scientias says late 2028, while an earlier museum announcement said mid-2028. In the meantime the museum's wharf and exhibition spaces stay open.

findings.question: How much does moving the Batavia onto land cost, and who is paying?
findings.answer: No figure for the move itself was found. Moving the ship ashore is part of a museum renovation and new-build worth about 25 million euros. The national government (Ministry of Education, Culture and Science and the Cultural Heritage Agency) pays 7 million euros for depots, the province of Flevoland 7.7 million for a new entrance and museum building, and the municipality of Lelystad 3.6 million for relocating the shipyard plus the land. Museum Batavialand raises up to 7 million through fundraising, sponsorship and loans guaranteed by the province.

events.name: Camera Japan Festival
events.when: Friday 2 October, 12:30–22:00 (festival runs Thursday 1 to Sunday 4 October)
events.blurb: The biggest Japanese film festival in the Benelux shows 19 films, including new arthouse films, anime, LGBTQ+ titles and classics, alongside Japanese art, music, dance and food. You can drop in any time in the afternoon or evening and see something on a big screen.
events.note: The festival says its 2026 dates and times could still change, so check the Camera Japan website before you go.

events.name: Benjamin Herman's European Alto Festival
events.blurb: Dutch saxophonist Benjamin Herman's festival pays tribute to the jazz legend Piet Noordijk. This year it features two international alto sax players, Spain's Irene Reig and Scotland's Rachael Cohen, with a piano, bass and drums trio. It's one night only at Amsterdam's best-known jazz venue, and you don't need any Dutch to enjoy it.

events.name: Afrovibes Festival
events.where: Vlaams Cultuurhuis de Brakke Grond, city centre
events.blurb: This is the 23rd year of the festival, which brings dance, theatre, music, spoken word and performance by artists from Africa and the African diaspora in the Netherlands. This year's theme is land, ancestry and belonging. It's a chance to see work that rarely gets a big stage.
events.note: The run at De Brakke Grond ends Saturday 3 October. The festival moves to Bijlmer Parktheater and Framer Framed on 3 and 4 October.
